Theme 019 · Typography & graphic systems

Guilloche Banknote Engraving

Every frame is printed like a banknote: interlacing guilloche rosettes, microtext borders, hatch-engraved serif numerals, a watermark window and coral serial numbers. Pulse is the UV lamp — it sweeps across each metric certificate, and on the one that is off, a ring of the rosette breaks in coral and hidden text lights up.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Guilloche rosette — concentric wavy rings and a spirograph core, generated as SVG paths in a teal rainbow ink.
  • Microtext border — repeating product words along the frame, the way banknotes hide text in their borders.
  • Engraved numeral — Instrument Serif filled with a diagonal hatch pattern plus a fine outline.
  • Watermark window — a clear oval in the rosette where the Acme mark appears as if held to light.
  • Serial number — coral mono numbering that counts per scene; the only warm color besides the anomaly.
  • UV band — a diagonal dark strip that reveals hidden fluorescent text: the context behind the anomaly.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Rosette draw — dash reveal while the ring phase advances, linear, a 4 s loop = two bars at 120 BPM.
  • UV sweep — the band crosses the certificate in 600 ms (power2.inOut) using a clip-path; it starts on a beat and lands on the next.
  • Serial roll — digits step per 16th note (125 ms) and lock on the downbeat when a scene settles.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Security printing is the visual language of "this can be trusted", and a broken ring in an otherwise perfect pattern is a very precise way to say "something here is off". It feels premium and calm. Risk: fine lines alias badly after compression — keep strokes around 2 px and use fewer, larger loops.

Adapt to your product: treat each object your product verifies (a payout, a certificate, a build, an identity check) as a note; generate the rosette from your own brand colors and put the evidence in the UV-revealed text.
